entities.summary:
Titus Ampius Balbus was a prominent Plebeian politician of Ancient Rome, born into the Ampia gens and living in the 1st century BCE. As the son of Titus, he rose to prominence through his family connections and political acumen. Balbus was a key figure in the tumultuous years leading up to the end of the Roman Republic, often cited by historian Cicero as the "trumpet of the Civil War".

Balbus's political career was marked by his involvement in the factional struggles of the late Roman Republic, where he often found himself at odds with his conservative opponents. Despite this, he managed to maintain a significant level of influence and support among his constituents, largely due to his reputation as a skilled orator and strategist. The exact dates of Balbus's life and political career are not well-documented, but it is known that he died in 100 BCE.

Balbus's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he played a significant role in shaping the course of Roman politics and history. His influence can be seen in the subsequent rise of the Roman Empire, where his own son would go on to play a key role in the early years of the imperial period.

The significance of Titus Ampius Balbus lies not only in his own political achievements but also in his role as a symbol of the tumultuous years leading up to the end of the Roman Republic. As such, he remains an important figure in the study of ancient Roman history and politics.
